finding.claim: SSRF in POST /profile/avatar. The only control is `startsWith("https://")`, which is not a host or IP allowlist. An attacker can target internal or metadata hosts that serve HTTPS, such as https://internal-host/ or https://169.254.169.254/. They can also point at an attacker-controlled HTTPS server that answers with a 302 to http://users.internal:8080/... or http://169.254.169.254/.... axios follows redirects by default (maxRedirects 5), and the redirect target is never re-validated, so the https-only restriction is bypassed. The response size is returned in `bytes`, which gives a blind oracle for internal resources. Impact: access to internal services and cloud metadata.
finding.source: req.body.avatarUrl (JSON body of POST /profile/avatar, any unauthenticated caller; no auth middleware exists)

trace.note: only check: typeof string and startsWith("https://"); no host/IP/DNS validation
axios.get(url) with default redirect following and no beforeRedirect hook
response length returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: The https:// prefix check is a scheme check only and is bypassed by redirects, internal HTTPS hosts and IP literals. No allowlist, private-IP blocking, maxRedirects:0, or auth was found. GET /users/:id (server.js:18-22) was checked as a sibling: the host is the constant USER_SVC and the id is encodeURIComponent'd, so it is SAFE for SSRF. Only path-level influence remains, and the host cannot be changed.

verdict.guard_found: none (only a scheme-prefix check, url.startsWith("https://"), at server.js:11)
verdict.reason: server.js:10 takes req.body.avatarUrl from an unauthenticated route with no auth middleware, server.js:11 only checks the "https://" prefix, and server.js:14 passes it to axios.get with default redirects, returning the byte length at server.js:15.
